reader.requirement: At 1985 the reference-modified unique data item is elementary without JUSTIFIED; a function slice is alphanumeric; a data-name-1 slice keeps data-name-1's class and category except that numeric, numeric edited and alphanumeric edited become alphanumeric, so an alphabetic slice stays alphabetic, and every rule keyed on category (MOVE validity, class condition, INITIALIZE) must see that category.

edition-consulted.switches: below 2002 the class condition takes the 1985 rule set (NumericNotAlphabeticOrSignedGroup1985, UsageDisplay1985, NotNumeric1985); at 2023 the 2023 set, which has no alphabetic bar on NUMERIC
--permissive only (not the edition): an alphabetic slice read as alphanumeric with a warning

reader.edition-search: grep of Place.cs, MoveTable16.cs, RefModBinder.cs for DialectLevel/CobolVersion/Edition: the category reader RefModPlace.CategoryOf is edition-invariant; the only edition switch reached is the class condition's rule set in ConditionBinder.CheckClassConditionOperand.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: 1985 bars the NUMERIC class test on an item described as alphabetic (VI.6.3.1.2 GR5) and the 2023 class condition has no such bar, so only at 1985 does an alphabetic slice's category decide a refusal of the class test
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness covers a numeric slice compared as characters; alphabetic slices, numeric edited and alphanumeric edited slices, the JUSTIFIED drop and the function arm are not exercised

reader.notes: MOVE (Table16Operand.Of(Place) with its alphabetic rider) and INITIALIZE (PB5813, landed) keep an alphabetic slice alphabetic, and numeric/edited slices are alphanumeric everywhere probed. The class condition does not: CheckClassConditionOperand reads the description through MoveTable16.OperandItem, which is null for a RefModPlace, and its comment says a slice is never alphabetic, citing §2023:8.4.3.3.4 GR6 c, a rewrite that names numeric only. Doubt: one could read VI.6.3.1.2's 'data description' as data-name-1's entry alone, but GR5 gives the slice that description's class and category.
